feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid public-sector alignment. It is well written overall, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, and it would be stronger with sharper outcomes and a cleaner structure.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership trajectory within NACo, showing promotion, increasing responsibility, and strong domain credibility in digital communications and platform modernization.  
- Good use of scale indicators and specifics: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms add impact.  
- Writing is polished and professional, with no obvious misspellings or major grammar errors; tone is consistent and senior-level.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and the footer projects; these sections overlap heavily and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond activity descriptions: e.g., improvements in engagement, efficiency, production capacity, search performance, or campaign results.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; capitalization varies slightly (“organization-wide” vs. other compounds), and “Coleman DAVIS” is visually inconsistent unless intentional branding.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning and clear seniority, but the intro is broad and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct, outcome-oriented language like “leading” or “modernizing” enterprise digital platforms and operations.
- Add one specific credibility marker from recent work, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” to ground the summary.
- Tighten the second sentence by grouping related areas: web modernization, governance, analytics, editorial workflows, and AI-enabled discovery.
- Consider rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web, governance, analytics, and editorial operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Leads complex, mission-driven digital ecosystems spanning large-scale Drupal platforms, multimedia production, and AI-enabled content discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; “AI-enabled content discovery” is more specific.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” repeats themes already covered in the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened into broader, less repetitive competency labels with parallel phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, category-style phrases and keep structure parallel; e.g.: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” for clearer meaning and stronger alignment with the AI search work.
- Consider “communications leadership” instead of “communications operations” to better reflect director-level scope.
- Standardize style by avoiding mixed constructions like “governance & editorial systems” vs. “multimedia production and livestream operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and Topline Skills; this section should stay high-level and avoid repeating tool-specific or project-specific language.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is already well established in the header and work experience.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work experience. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it feel more distinct and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” framing to reinforce recency and separate this from core experience.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: start each item with a strong verb and trim stacked nouns (e.g., “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and AI chat”).
- Clarify audience/value where possible: “for legislative/policy users,” “for member engagement,” or “to support ongoing campaign expansion.”
- Standardize style: use “10 x 20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot,” and consider “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video work substantially repeat achievements already covered in recent roles; consider making these more outcome-focused or visually briefer.
- “Built/Developed” repeats across all entries; vary verbs to avoid monotony.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope and good alignment to your headline, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around 3–5 outcomes and distinguish it from your NACo leadership roles by emphasizing consulting impact, Drupal delivery, and AI search.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into outcome-focused lines, e.g.:
- Built Drupal campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content sections, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved digital operations by designing cross-team workflows, analytics/reporting processes, and governance standards across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative covering retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user-facing discovery experience.
- Add metrics where possible: number of sites/pages/users, publishing time reduced, toolkit downloads, search success, engagement lift.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps with the 2022–2024 NACo role; keep this entry more implementation- and project-delivery-focused.
- The AI search and microsite work also appears in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and multi-channel communications across web, email, social, and video.”
- Rewrite bullets to emphasize outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: for email/social, include growth, engagement, open/click rates, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements if available.
- Tighten weaker phrasing: change “expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure” to “implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting stack, improving leadership visibility and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version more strategic and less operational.
- Video leadership may overlap with older NACo entries; focus here on building the in-house studio and organizational capacity, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a summary than an impact-focused accomplishment set. Sharpen it around scope, channel ownership, and systems/process improvements that distinguish it from the later director role.

Suggested edit
- Open with ownership + scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets to action + outcome: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more results-oriented: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a repeatable policy communications channel.”
- Reframe process bullets with stronger verbs: “Built cross-team editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving publishing coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “digital communications across web, email, social media and video” duplicates the Director of Digital Media entry; emphasize execution/coordination here, not overall leadership.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the prior role and footer project list; position this as scaling/formalizing the series.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent experience. It should be tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership scope rather than restating broad digital/communications terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, executive-level wording tied to current positioning.
- Keep to 4 bullets max and use parallel phrasing.
- Suggested rewrite:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance, publishing systems, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging strategy
- If space allows, swap “audience-focused content planning” for “audience-centered content strategy” to sound more senior and less tactical.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with both the header summary and multiple NACo experience bullets.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent web modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Prioritize recent/relevant platforms; keep Drupal first, and consider dropping or de-emphasizing older/general platforms unless they are job-target critical.
- Replace “Power Pages” and “SharePoint” here if they are not central to recent roles; save them for Technical + IT.
- If space allows, make one item more outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-facing sites” or “AI-enabled search and discovery experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; Topline Skills should stay higher-level.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies, so avoid repeating exact phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to outcomes-oriented capabilities, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Keep only the most important platforms here and group them tightly: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Analytics strategy & optimization — GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • KPI design • Executive reporting • SEO and digital performance analysis”
- If you have proof points, align wording to recent impact: “enterprise analytics infrastructure,” “leadership dashboards,” or “decision-support reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; use Topline Skills for strategic framing, and leave full tool inventory in Technical + IT.
- “Leadership reporting” may read weaker than “executive reporting” or “leadership dashboards.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Make it more senior and outcomes-oriented by emphasizing production leadership and delivery environments rather than listing basic capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Live Event Delivery**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level bullets:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production  
- Livestream and hybrid event production  
- PTZ camera and in-house studio operations  
- Virtual event delivery and technical run-of-show coordination
- If accurate, strengthen with scope language such as: “multi-camera,” “broadcast-quality,” or “end-to-end production.”
- Keep tool-specific items like Premiere Pro/Audition out of this section since they already appear under Technical + IT.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “multimedia production” already appear in Core Competencies; use this section to add nuance, not repeat the same phrasing.
- “Video production and editing” overlaps with Technical + IT; avoid sounding too tactical here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either add context (level/relevance) or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize by recency/strength: lead with Drupal, then WordPress/SharePoint; move GitHub Pages last or remove if not materially used.
- Consider adding proficiency framing: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint/Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, group lower-priority tools: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint / Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Best option if keeping this section: align to current work impact, e.g. “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages” and let project bullets show outcomes.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates Topline Skills [2] almost exactly; consider deleting one version or making this item more technical/platform-specific while Topline Skills stays broader.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent experience and projects, so avoid over-listing it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should emphasize implementation tools not already covered elsewhere and use cleaner, more current phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Tighten and modernize the list: **HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Remove **jQuery** unless it is still actively used in recent work; if retained, place it last or label it **legacy support**.
- If space allows, add specificity tied to recent work: **front-end implementation, deployment automation, serverless scripting, tag management**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations** already appear under **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep them in one place or make this version more implementation-focused.
- **Workflow automation** is covered elsewhere, so avoid implying GitHub Actions duplicates that broader category.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation & project systems: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; Slack, Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most differentiating tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier should lead because they align with your recent systems/governance work.
- Consider trimming lower-signal collaboration tools unless they were admin/implementation responsibilities; Slack and Teams can feel generic.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier for impact: “Used to build editorial planning, intake, approval and cross-team coordination workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp all signal project management—listing all four may feel redundant unless each was meaningfully used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platforms to include, but this item is too bare and reads like a vendor list. It should signal level of use and align with the strong email/communications leadership already shown in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and standardize naming: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show applied use without repeating work-history detail: **Enterprise email campaign delivery, newsletter operations and audience engagement**
- If one platform was primary, order by strongest/recentest use rather than alphabetically.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; keep this section tool-focused, not responsibility-focused.
- Avoid adding broad phrases like “multi-channel communications” here, since that already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, tighten it to platforms/methods and make the wording more precise.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI/dashboard development**
- Swap **SEO** for **Google Search Console** or **SEO/performance analysis**; “SEO” alone reads broad/non-technical.
- Change **Dashboarding** to **KPI/dashboard development** or **reporting automation** for stronger, more specific phrasing.
- If space allows, order by depth/relevance from recent roles: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Power BI • Looker Studio • BigQuery ...**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**. Consider keeping the topline section outcome-oriented and this section tool-only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role; avoid repeating extra descriptors here unless they add specificity.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content production, and any concrete scale/results.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital media team…”
- Tighten scope and reduce generic phrasing: replace “strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia” with specific contributions such as production coordination, publishing processes, or channel operations.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: size of website refresh, frequency/audience of livestreams or weekly videos, number of channels supported, or team size.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped build NACo’s first in-house digital media team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day publishing and production workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Provided informal supervision and guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching/early production rather than expansion.
- Avoid repeating governance/workflow language already used more strongly in later roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially launching the first podcast. It should be tightened and framed around distinct contributions so it doesn’t overlap too much with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the strongest differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast…”
- Replace generic phrases like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with clearer scope and purpose.
- Split research/program support from media work to show range without sounding vague.
- Suggested rewrite: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams. Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications, and launched NACo’s first podcast—leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on the podcast launch and innovation/research support.
- Avoid broad claims about digital leadership here, since stronger, more recent evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. Tighten it to emphasize current, professional production tools and align wording with the stronger multimedia leadership already shown in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Separate tools from capabilities for cleaner scanning: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream production • Podcast production”
